hook_text: Ten fingers, one fold, and 9 times 7 appears. Here is why it is not magic.
clip_script: Hold up ten fingers. 9 times 7? Fold down finger number 7. Six on the left, three on the right. 63. Try 9 times 4: fold the fourth. Three and six. 36. Why does it work? Nine is ten minus one. 9 times 7 is 70 minus 7. The six fingers are six tens, 60. The three fingers are the leftover units. Every 9 times answer has digits that add to 9: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81. Now the facts that trip everyone: 6 times 7 is 42. 7 times 8 is 56. 6 times 8 is 48. Say them today, say them tomorrow, and by next week they are yours. Every fact has a twin, so 7 times 6 comes free with 6 times 7. Tables are not a mountain. They are a short list and a few tricks.
visual_style: Whiteboard pair of hands with one finger folding; digits of the 9 times answers highlighted adding to 9; a short list of hard facts ticked off.
mood: Playful, a little showing off, then reassuring.
pacing: Two finger-trick demos, the quick why, the hard-fact list, then the twin rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and teach the finger trick to someone at home tonight.
